subject.title: Feature: Distinguish webchat client types (Mac app vs browser)

question: Should WebChat client type become agent-visible as gateway-attested metadata, explicitly untrusted diagnostic metadata, or remain hidden from the model context?
rationale: Current Gateway clients already self-report rich metadata, but exposing it to agents changes the security boundary because models may use it for native-only behavior or debugging decisions.

options.title: Expose sanitized metadata with trust semantics
options.body: Reuse `connect.client` fields, mark which values are gateway/device-attested versus client-declared, and add focused prompt/context tests before implementation.

options.title: Expose untrusted diagnostics only
options.body: Allow client type only as a labeled diagnostic hint so agents and tools cannot treat it as an authorization or capability signal.

options.title: Decline runtime exposure for now
options.body: Keep the existing Gateway logging metadata and avoid model-visible client identity until a stronger attestation or capability contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Expose sanitized metadata with trust semantics
recommendation.body: Reuse `connect.client` fields, mark which values are gateway/device-attested versus client-declared, and add focused prompt/context tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent work across Gateway client protocol, chat context, Control UI, and native Gateway connection code.
